findings.title: Panic due to uninitialized quota map
findings.description: The `quota` map in `Store` is never initialized in `NewStore`, causing a panic when `Create` attempts to increment an owner's quota.

findings.title: Deadlock in cache eviction
findings.description: The `evict` method holds a write lock and calls `Get`, which attempts to acquire a read lock on the same mutex, resulting in an immediate deadlock.

findings.title: Panic in CheckTargets on request failure
findings.description: If `mustHead` fails to create a request, it returns `nil`. Passing `nil` to `client.Do` causes a runtime panic.

findings.title: Inverted link expiry logic
findings.description: In `Resolve`, the condition `time.Now().Before(l.ExpiresAt)` checks if a link is still valid. If true, it deletes the link and returns `ErrNotFound`, effectively killing valid links and preserving expired ones.

findings.title: Impossible condition in RequireAdmin
findings.description: The check `s.Role != "admin" || s.Role != "owner"` is a tautology; it is always true regardless of the role, meaning no user can ever pass the admin check.

findings.title: Slice bounds panic in Page
findings.description: The `end` index is set to `len(all) + 1` when the requested size exceeds remaining items, causing a panic when slicing `all[offset:end]`.

findings.title: Metrics not updated due to value receiver
findings.description: The `AddResolved` method uses a value receiver `(m Metrics)`, meaning it increments a copy of the metrics rather than the instance held by the server.

findings.title: Incorrect TTL unit in configuration
findings.description: The environment variable `LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS` suggests milliseconds, but the code multiplies the value by `time.Second`.

findings.title: HTTP response body leak in preview
findings.description: The response body from `s.client.Get(target)` is never closed, leading to a resource leak of socket handles.

findings.title: Division by zero in stats
findings.description: If `links` is empty, `hits / int64(len(links))` will cause a division by zero panic.

findings.title: Data race on Store maps
findings.description: The Store's 'links' and 'quota' maps are accessed and mutated concurrently by multiple HTTP handler goroutines without any synchronization, which will lead to runtime panics.

findings.title: Data race on Authenticator sessions map
findings.description: The Authenticator's 'sessions' map is read during verification and mutated during issuance/revocation concurrently across requests without synchronization.

findings.title: Map deletion under RLock
findings.description: Cache.Get calls 'delete(c.m, code)' while holding a read lock (RLock). Map mutations require a full Lock; this will cause a data race or panic.

findings.title: Goroutine leak in CheckTargets
findings.description: CheckTargets returns immediately on the first error encountered. Because the 'results' channel is unbuffered, all other pending probe goroutines will block forever attempting to send their results, leaking goroutines.

findings.title: Mutex copied by value in AddResolved
findings.description: AddResolved uses a value receiver (m Metrics), which copies the mutex. Locking a copy does not protect the original object, rendering the synchronization useless.

findings.title: WaitGroup Add race in WarmCache
findings.description: wg.Add(1) is called inside the goroutine. wg.Wait() may execute and return before any goroutines have started, causing the function to return before work is done.

findings.title: Deadlock in Cache.evict
findings.description: Cache.evict holds a write Lock and calls Cache.Get, which attempts to acquire an RLock. This can deadlock if other writers are waiting for the lock.

findings.title: Data race in StartJanitor
findings.description: The janitor goroutine iterates over s.links without synchronization while other goroutines are mutating the map via Store methods.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in preview endpoint
findings.description: The /preview/{code} endpoint fetches the content of the target URL using the server's HTTP client. An attacker can create a short link pointing to internal infrastructure (e.g., http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) and use the preview endpoint to exfiltrate sensitive internal data.

findings.title: Broken Access Control in link deletion
findings.description: The Delete method in store.go removes a link based solely on the provided code, without verifying that the requester is the owner of the link. An attacker can delete any short link in the system by guessing or discovering its code.

findings.title: Predictable session tokens via math/rand
findings.description: The Issue method uses math/rand.Intn to generate session tokens. Because math/rand is a pseudo-random number generator, an attacker who observes a sequence of tokens can predict future tokens and hijack user sessions.

findings.title: Open Redirect in /out endpoint
findings.description: The /out endpoint redirects users to the URL provided in the 'next' query parameter without any validation. This can be exploited to create deceptive links that appear to belong to the trusted service but redirect users to malicious phishing sites.

findings.title: Path Traversal in report export
findings.description: The /report endpoint passes the 'name' query parameter directly to ExportCSV, which uses filepath.Join to construct the output path. An attacker can provide a name like '../../etc/passwd' to write files outside the intended export directory.

findings.title: Denial of Service via panic in BearerToken
findings.description: The BearerToken function attempts to access index 1 of the split authorization header without checking if the header is present or contains a space. A request with a missing or malformed Authorization header will cause the server to panic and crash.

findings.title: Insecure Administrative Authentication
findings.description: The /admin/quotas endpoint relies on the presence of the 'X-Admin: true' header for authentication. Since HTTP headers can be easily spoofed by any client, this provides no real security for administrative functions.

findings.title: Insecure CORS configuration
findings.description: The writeJSON function sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This combination is insecure as it allows any website to make authenticated requests to the API on behalf of the user.

findings.title: Weak password hashing without salt
findings.description: HashPassword uses a single round of SHA256 without a salt. This makes passwords vulnerable to rainbow table attacks and precomputed hash lookups.

findings.title: Session token leakage in error messages
findings.description: The authentication middleware echoes the provided token back to the user in the 401 Unauthorized error response. This can lead to tokens being leaked in client logs or intercepted by intermediaries.

findings.title: Imprecise owner lookup in ByOwner
findings.description: The ByOwner method uses strings.Contains to filter links by owner. This allows a search for a short owner name to return links belonging to other users whose names contain that string.
